body.estimand_functional: \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\vartheta\in\Theta:\inf_{c\in\mathcal G_c}\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)\le\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\},\quad L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n\text{ by the proposed upper comparison only on }\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\)

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and an unknown law-specific cutoff \(c_P\in[1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.units: The observations are \(O_i=(X_i,D_i,Y_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with binary treatment and outcome.
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument is \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge c_P\}\), and monotone response types imply \(D_i=D_i(Z_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The compliance jump lies in \([\kappa_n,2\kappa_n]\). The main class imposes no outcome-variance, residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor; every binary treatment--outcome association compatible with the observable margins and causal model is allowed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Separate one-sided radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions are imposed only on the observable treatment and outcome margins. Association is a free binwise Fr\'echet coordinate. A four-cell method-of-types threshold gives finite-sample calibration on certified grids, and the rule returns the full parameter space on each enumerated fallback branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 establishes honesty of the bias-aware Anderson--Rubin confidence set at a known cutoff.
Their weak-identification-robust fuzzy-RD procedure inverts a reduced-form test at a fixed known cutoff.
Their unknown-threshold result transfers the minimax rate for estimating a sharp-RD discontinuity location from a convolution white-noise model.
Their moderate-break analysis derives a Gaussian-process limit experiment and a nearly weighted-average-power maximizing test.
Their Theorem 1 gives uniformly asymptotically valid conditional tests with a functional nuisance parameter.
Their Theorem 1 shows that risk functions attainable in the weak-GMM Gaussian-process experiment bound finite-sample asymptotic risk.
Their Theorem 3.1 characterizes optimal one-sided confidence intervals through an ordered modulus over convex fixed-index regression classes.
Their sharp testable implications for fuzzy-RD validity are inequalities in the joint outcome--treatment distribution at the cutoff.
Their LoTTA model propagates posterior uncertainty about an unknown cutoff into fuzzy-RD effect estimation.
Their main unknown-discontinuity theory treats testing and estimation in sharp RD, with fuzzy RD discussed separately.

body.tldr: For fuzzy regression discontinuity with a weak compliance jump and unknown cutoff, cutoff recovery and causal-effect informativeness are distinct. A legal moving-cutoff continuum yields the exact flat-face limit \(2(1-\alpha)\), while \(T_n\), \(\tau_n\), and \(\lambda_n\) give an explicit all-strength regime partition. The open kernel is the \(s=1\) critical decision value and a total support-wide interval based on a formally defined four-cell population profile. Finite-grid calibration covers every compatible treatment--outcome association, including singular cells. When \(c_P\) is supplied, the singleton cutoff grid gives conditional and unconditional coverage at least \(1-\delta_n\) provided \(\theta_P\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and the certified outer program contains the true bin averages; no continuum-honesty, expected-length, or first-order-equivalence claim is made for this fixed-cutoff reduction. The conservative unknown-cutoff procedure's upper rate is posed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), where its named grid, sieve, stochastic, continuum-transfer, calibration, and fallback errors are negligible.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy inference, sharp-RD unknown-cutoff rates, generic weak-identification decision theory, and Bayesian propagation of cutoff uncertainty have been developed separately. None characterizes honest connected-interval length when the cutoff and fuzzy denominator weaken jointly.
project_justification.niche: The preserved binary uniform-design class makes the causal lift explicit while leaving the observable treatment--outcome association unrestricted. This creates a nonregular location/effect decision problem that is neither a fixed-boundary modulus problem nor a parametric unknown-break problem.
project_justification.fill: The project couples a legal moving-cutoff continuum with a support-wide four-cell population profile and a coarsened exact calibration that leaves association free. It evaluates the critical decision problems and seeks a total honest interval, with its conservative finite-grid upper-rate claim confined to the explicitly certifiable recovered regime.

body.related_work: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the local Wald identification argument. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) are the direct weak-identification fuzzy-RD predecessor: their reduced-form inversion treats the assignment cutoff as fixed and known, so there is no cutoff/effect-label experiment or unknown-cutoff minimax connected-length problem. Noack and Rothe (2024, Theorem 1 and Assumption 1(iii)) provide known-cutoff bias-aware inversion under conditions supporting studentization. The proved known-cutoff benchmark here is deliberately narrower: setting \(\mathcal G_c=\{c_P\}\) specializes the binned four-cell method-of-types test and yields conditional and unconditional finite-grid coverage when \(\theta_P\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and the certified outer program contains the true bin averages. It claims neither continuum honesty, an expected-length rate, nor first-order equivalence to residual-jump inversion. Porter and Yu (2015, Sections 3--5) and Tuvaandorj (2020, Sections 3--4) inform unknown-location analysis in predominantly sharp designs, without the weak causal ratio. Elliott and M\"uller (2014, Sections 2.1--2.3) show why moderate unknown breaks require a process experiment, but their parametric break problem has no H\"older recovery profile. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, equations (3)--(4) and Theorem 1) and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022, Theorem 1 and Section 4) inform nuisance calibration and weak-decision analysis. Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.4) connect testing power to expected length over convex fixed-index classes; the cutoff-indexed class here is a translated nonconvex union. Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022, Section 2) establish that fuzzy-RD validity restrictions reside in the joint outcome--treatment law, motivating retention of all four observed cells. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version, Sections 3 and 6) propagate unknown-cutoff uncertainty in a Bayesian model without uniform frequentist honesty or minimax length.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A product of the two marginal Bernoulli likelihoods is not the likelihood of the observed pair when association is unrestricted. The finite-grid calibration therefore uses the complete binned four-cell vector and a method-of-types threshold that remains valid on singular cell faces. Its dimension cost \(\zeta_n\) need not be negligible on every sequence satisfying cutoff recovery; the stated upper-rate comparison is therefore confined to \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), while a sharper association-robust calibration for the remainder of \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\) stays open. Separately, an untruncated second moment of a translated-cutoff mixture does not determine a critical constant; boundary truncation, mixture renormalization, the signed effect label, and second-order centering must remain in the experiment.
body.honest_scope: The main class has no outcome-variance, null-residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor. The known-cutoff theorem proves finite-grid calibration only: it requires \(\theta_P\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and containment of the true bin averages in the certified outer program, and it makes no continuum-honesty, expected-length, or first-order-equivalence claim. Its coverage is nevertheless uniform over all permitted binary treatment--outcome associations, including zero cells and singular residuals. The proved results are the legal moving-cutoff continuum and causal lift, its finite-sample Kullback--Leibler bound, the flat-face expected-length limit, the algebraic regime partition, a population false-split lower bound, and exact finite-grid four-cell calibration. The false-split bound and grid calibration do not establish a continuum all-strength profile interval or its expected-length risk. The finite-positive decision values, full-model least favorability, continuum discretization, negligible fallback risk, and all-strength attainment are open-ended questions. The minimax lower comparison at scale \(r_n\) is posed on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\); the conservative finite-grid upper comparison is posed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\). No smoothness of joint cells, conditional independence, association separation, cross-side derivative matching, oracle cutoff, or known association nuisance is imposed.
